title: Oracle POS System Could be a Game-Changer
description: Today, digital systems have become an operator’s best friend. Gone are the days of the chunky cash register that were permanently stuck in designated areas of the restaurant. Now point-of-sale (POS) tablets and handheld devices are becoming wildly popular at restaurants.  These POS systems have morphed into state-of-the-art tools that offer much more than just a solution to collect customer transactions. Packed with features, these solutions enhance a restaurant’s day-to-day operations, while also helping the operator understand their customers better.  On this episode of On Foodable Weekly, we take a closer look at one of the most innovative systems out there, the Oracle Simphony POS software.   ⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺⎺  More Foodable Shows ➜ https://t2m.io/OnDemand-Foodable  Subscribe on YouTube :check mark: https://goo.gl/m77X78  ───────────────────────────  Foodable Network ➜ https://goo.gl/aTTdMi Facebook ➜ https://goo.gl/R4TjXz Twitter ➜ https://goo.gl/jHvE1H

asr.full_text: Restaurant technology has grown and improved drastically over the last few years. POS technology is one of the fastest evolving platforms in food service today from inventory to social to knowing your guest point of sale is becoming a one stop solution for more than just your transactions. New restaurant technologies are taking lessons from consumer technologies to improve customer experience for North America at Oracle Hospitality. This is a very exciting space where what we've done is to couple our cafeteria with meeting rooms and demonstration areas for technology. So as guests arrive, they're able to really get a feel for how our technology interacts within the hotel and food and beverage space. You know, when I look back 10 years ago, tablet devices, hand-held devices, were a great idea, but they weren't taking on, the adoption was very low. So we've seen dramatic changes as consumer-based devices have taken hold in the general population, is now making it its way into merchant use devices. You're seeing mobility as a really key component for technology advancement. You're seeing cloud infrastructure as a way to take technology out of the local establishments and reduce that complexity so that focus can be attached to the guest experience and not to managing IT. I think as the prices come down, as the software has coupled better with the hardware, as Wi-Fi has become more secure, all these things are coming together at a perfect time in addition to robotics and self-ordering automation that is bringing the consumer more into a power position to manage their own transactions. this is where technology all comes together, but it has to be thoughtfully implemented. And that is where our consulting services work hard to understand the dynamics of our customers and how to introduce new technology that will provide ROI. We really focus on the business justification of technology, not just the delivery of it. So the workspace 6 was built with a few things in mind. Number one we wanted to make sure that we would service and support it for years to come. Number two that it'd have to be ultra-reliable and flexible. That it would have all the ports that you would need for future connectivity to peripherals that we may or may not need right away and that the design would be such that it would be resistant to spills and grease and dirt grime and be able to take hits in the environment. So this purpose built device, which also has the ability to run off the stand, it could be wall mounted, it could be kiosk mounted, it could be in the kitchen as a kitchen display unit. Makes it really versatile and reliable. This hardware was designed to work with Oracle's Symfony Platform. What makes Symfony really exciting is that we're no longer reliant on a server in the restaurant. We're no longer relying on having to do upgrades on that server or to have people come on site and charge money in order to do those upgrades. So you're always able to keep your technology fresh, you're able to keep your CapEx expenditures down. There's an operating expense that you're following within a subscription, but it's controllable, it's budgetable. By delivering our applications over the internet through the cloud, not only are we able to upgrade software very easily but we are also able to deliver training specific to the particular customer. What we are trying to do is to leverage Synphony as the platform that will allow our customers to be in position to take advantage of these emerging technologies through both what we develop as well as what our partners integrate with us. The idea of future-proofing hardware is challenging because of all the changes that occur but we kind of know what we need the hardware to do after being in business for over 30. We need to be able to adapt to peripheral device connectivity. Today, it might be scanners and scale. Tomorrow, it could be fingerprint readers that become more ubiquitous. It could be infrared technology. It could be all print readers that become more ubiquitous, it could be infrared technology it could be all types of different things. We gotta make sure we've got the ports and the connections for that. And typically you'll see in a Workstation 6 that that's how it is built. One of the key attributes of the Workstation 6 application design with Symfony is something we call CAL, Client Application Loader. And what that means is you simply connect the device and download from the internet all of the attributes that the workstation 6 needs to learn to run Symfony. So the CAL allows us to provide service to you, or for you to even do self-service if you had an extra workstation around, it's very simple to simply swap out a device and put a new one in. So it's built against the environment and it's built to last more than a few years in the harshness of the restaurant world. So the application really needs to fit with the hardware so that we could take our workstation 6 and we can make it a cashier workstation, we can make it a self order workstation, we can make it a kitchen display unit. When looking at mobile devices that tablet devices we've been through many generations over the years, there's been an adoption issue because we really haven't had the right killer form factor for a tablet. We think we solve this with the Tablet 720. With the Tablet 720, we've got enough real estate that we can mimic the workstation design and screen flow of this workstation 6 so the training issues don't become a problem. It allows you manages conversational ordering or dynamic ordering at table sides. What that means is that you're able to correct orders easily, including modifications. And the tablet design is built for six to eight hour battery life but if you should lose the power in the middle of the shift, you simply swap the battery out... and you're off from running again. And lastly one of the thoughtful things that we did because people are worried about breakage, is to put together a nifty little pouch that allows you when you're finished taking your order with the nifty little strap to put it into your holster and to go on and do your work. The Symphony was built from thester and to go on to do your work. The Symphony was built from the ground up to focus on the hospitality environment. When people are hungry, when people want to have fun, in the food and beverage and hotel industry, they don't want to have an eruption. We had to have an ultra reliable system. So what we built the system to do would be to run off the internet, so we don't depend on our hosting center to run symphony transactions, we download what we need, we pull down what we need from the application in the in the hosting center and if we should lose connection to the internet or to the data center we're able to keep operating on our workstations and run transactions so guest service is not interrupted, that was a critical element in the design of Symphony. You know, on a personal level when you think about your own dining experiences you probably only have seven or eight places that you go to a lot and why is that such a small number? And what is it about that finite number of places that you most frequent that makes you wanna come back? and what would a restaurateur have to do to attract you to make you one of their one of their chosen few they like to have an experience in value and and what is that mean that music combination quality and price and getting what they expect and technology can be asked for a really tremendous underpinning to support that value proposition that each of our customers offers. So by making sure that the focus is on the customer, and the guest's experience, the guest's engagement is critical, and the food is delivered fresh on time the way it's expected consistently. So technology should never be in the way but should always be driving the way the our customers are able to deliver that value to their customers. It can be difficult to keep up with the evolution of these technologies and the companies that are finding ways to stay ahead of the curve. Be sure to download the Foodable Tech Guide for more insights on the latest in restaurant technology.
